steps.text: Our sister, Hildegard. Today, we see you off.
May the light extol your path forth, may piety and conviction be forever by your side.
The bells of Landen Monastery cross long through... hm? What?
*cough* The bells of Landen Monastery cross long through the years, tolling centuries of... Wine!?
Wh—Why has wine been left here? Where did... my Lord, don't tell me the old man snuck it in? Shh! Sshhh!
To be brief, may Landen's centuries of glory be with you! Now, Hildegard! Come here and help! Help us get the wine barrel open!
Hee-hee, we can't have a farewell without this, can we? Now, before the old man comes back! Cheers!

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Ah... did I fall asleep?

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Someone's knocking at the door... it's this late already!?

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: Good morning, Cleric Hildegard.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Good morning, or should I say good afternoon, Mr. Bison. It's been long since I laid on a bed. I seem to be somewhat remiss.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: It's been a long journey, I don't blame you. I came to confirm your travel itinerary today; hopefully I didn't disturb your rest?

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: No worries at all. I thank all your efforts as well.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: You came from Laterano... such a far-off country, all the way to Lungmen. It can't have been easy, can it?

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: It wasn't.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: This is my own first time so far from Laterano... Long-distance travel isn't as simple as admiring the scenery, it turns out.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: Ha ha. Even seasoned Messengers still take every method they can to keep their moods level...

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: The life of a Messenger must be tough.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: So, Miss Hildegard, was last night's accommodation to your liking?

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Mm-hm. It's a stone's throw from the city center, and very cheaply priced. You've got some keen insight.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: You don't need to worry about expenses, actually. MountainDash Logistics will reimburse the costs of your time in Lungmen.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: No, as a representative of Landen Monastery, I can't depend on the wealth of others. Forgive me for that.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: What's more, I'm on this mission precisely to address the many problems besetting the Monastery. I could never partake excessively of others' friendship on their land, all while indulging myself.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: I see... your mindset really is admirable.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: A compulsory lesson, and nothing more.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: Your meeting with Eurill is set for tomorrow evening. May I ask what your plans are for today?

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Um... I'll take a small walk around the area. It's my first time in Yan, after all.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: Will you require a tour guide or entourage to be arranged, then?

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Ah, no. I'd like to look about myself. I'm just satisfying my own curiosity, that's all; I wouldn't like to trouble you all.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: Alright... then I won't keep bothering you.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Thank you for your understanding.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: If I may be so bold as to ask, Mr. Eurill is your father, is he not?

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: Hm? Uh, he is. What about it?

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: No, forgive me. It's just that I've noticed you treat him wholly as if he's your boss while you're on the job, Mr. Bison...

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: Uh-huh. If I always rely on my relationship with the old man, how could I ever surpass him?

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Hahah, I see you're someone of great ambitions too, then, Mr. Bison.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: Hardly. If it hadn't come up with you, Cleric Hildegard, I wouldn't even talk about anything like it with a client.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: Well, I won't bother you any further...

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: But if you have any spare time, I'd like to hear your stories about Laterano. Just as you're curious about Lungmen, I... think about that place a lot.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: But of course.

steps.name: Bison
steps.text: Alright. I wish you a pleasant day.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Lungmen, then.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: I don't really have any travel funds, but... I suppose I'll wander around some.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: After all, 'opportunity and faith alike dwell in markets and bells.'

steps.name: Male Lungmenite
steps.text: Your dad's too set in his ways! This is Lungmen, come on!

steps.name: Female Lungmenite
steps.text: But it's a craft our old place passed down from generation to generation...

steps.name: Male Lungmenite
steps.text: Look at the age we're in now! How's manual labor going to make any money?

steps.name: Female Lungmenite
steps.text: That's true. That's something my dad needs to be talked over for.

steps.name: Male Lungmenite
steps.text: What number were we in the queue again?

steps.name: Female Lungmenite
steps.text: Number 21. It'll be us pretty soon now. Why's this dessert shop so crowded...

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: I'm number 31.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: So sweet...

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Huh...?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Uh... a-are you the visitor from Laterano?

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Hm? Do you know of me?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Uh, yes, actually, for certain reasons my house is currently uninhabitable, so the L.G.D. gave me a residence at the same inn as you... erm, I'm actually right across from you...

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: So I see... what a coincidence, then.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Ah, where are my manners? I should introduce myself first. I come from Laterano's Landen Monastery. Please, call me Hildegard. You might be?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Y-Y-You don't need to be all polite to me, I'm just an average engineer... engineer, codename Snowsant...

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Actually, um, why isn't a person of your status living in a more high-class apartment instead?

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Ahahah... I have a few troubles, too, but it's moreso to remind myself. You needn't be so modest with me, either. I'm just touring around right now, that's all.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Here. Would you like some?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Are these... cakes?

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: I'd noticed they were famous, and so I bought two extra, but I hadn't imagined the flavor would be so intense.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: That said, if such things can gain widespread popularity, then perhaps the goods the Monastery can offer may not suit Lungmen...

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Are you sure you can give me these?!

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Eh? Ah, by all means.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Th... thank you...

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: (She's just like a hungry little cystybeast...) Ahem. Do eat a little slower.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Snowsant, was it? Would you be able to accompany me for a while longer?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Nmp, *sigh*. Of... Of course, Ma'am! I'm on vacation today!

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: D—Don't shout 'Ma'am' like that; I feel a little bad now...

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: I hadn't noticed, but it's already evening now.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: The days without hearing the bells...

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Miss Hildegard, is something wrong?

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Ah. Nothing. I just feel like the time passes so fast.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: In the end, today was a day off, and the traffic jams were all so bad. We just wandered around Lungmen city center a little and it's already dark now.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Snowsant, what kind of place is Columbia, I wonder?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Huh? Let me think... uh, everything's so bright all the time, it's really technological, and...

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: A little inhuman...?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: O-Of course, I only stayed in the research institute! To be clear, I never went more than two kilometers from my workplace!

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Ohh, that tiny little back-and-forth life... I feel queasy...

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Hahah... forget I mentioned it. Don't force yourself.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Sigh.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Miss Hildegard, what kind of... place is Landen Monastery? I've only heard about the Notarial Hall before...

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: ...Bread.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Bread?

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: It's ancient, a convent situated amongst the wheat fields and hills.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: It was originally for the training of Apostolic warriors. Its greatest difference from the Notarial Hall and the Apostolic Knights is that Landen Monastery accepts people from countries the world over.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Gulp. But..?

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: But these last few years have been too peaceful! The Notarial Hall mopped up every last bit of our work! We didn't get a single new disciple this year! The old man's cohort refuses any grants on the grounds of teaching the Monastery to be self-reliant!

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: It's about to go bankrupt. The time-honored Landen Monastery is about to go BANKRUPT because of its financial issues!!

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Miss Hildegard, should you say 'bankrupt' for a monastery...?

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: It's the closest word there is. Take it or leave it.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: *cough* *cough*.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: And that's why you left Laterano, Miss Hildegard?

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: There always has to be a way. Fortunately, the Monastery's reputation aside, people might not think we're much more than ornamental, but at the very least, we still have our grand wheat field...

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: I've troubled you enough for today, Snowsant.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: N-No problem! I didn't have any other plans for today anyway...

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: I'm in Room 152! If there's anything else you need, Miss, you can come to me... Until my house is done being cleaned up, I'll be living here the whole time!

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: Ah, Cleric Hildegard, welcome.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Mr. Eurill, the privilege is mine.

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: Not at all. Loosen up, Cleric Hildegard, we're not too fond of overly formal meetings in our corporate culture.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Alright, then...

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: So. Regarding the business terms, coming from Landen Monastery to Lungmen—

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: You're impressive. You had everything planned and prepared well in advance. Today was actually just to tell me about it all, wasn't it?

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: Nonsense.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Truly perfect. With my current insight alone, I have no way to compare to you in terms of Messenger-related work.

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: Hah hah hah, it's my honor to get the seal of approval from a Laterano monastery cleric.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Mr. Eurill, forgive me for being so bold, but I'd like to ask you a few personal questions.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Why choose Landen Monastery?

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: If a company with the heft of MountainDash Logistics seeks to open Messenger channels and refine its procedures...

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: Nonsense. We're deeply honored to be able to cooperate with an establishment as long and storied as Landen Monastery.

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: —Do you know what the limit of my logistics company's reach is?

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: As proud as I am of MountainDash Logistics, it's got no footprint beyond Lungmen and the five cities of Yan around it.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: What about Ursus, or Victoria? Lungmen is a crucial outwards-facing hub for Yan, so shouldn't foreign...

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: Unlike what the average person on the street thinks, it's damned hard for a logistics company to operate anywhere outside of its country of registration.

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: Even with fully lawful transit, most civil logistics business still gets passed onto locally partnered Messenger orgs afterwards. Not a single country's so loose it'd let other nations' Messengers run free range on its own soil.

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: Of course... that's just 'over-the-table' modes of work, but we don't need to probe into any sort of gray area right about now. Don't you mind it.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: I see, then...

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: It's exactly as you say. For the stable setup of all kinds of information and transport hub links, the costs are—yes—not at all proportional to the profits the Monastery's goods bring in.

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: Even the cost of setting up a single Catastrophe Messenger base station'd blow your socks off.

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: However, this piece of business is a pathway connecting us to Laterano. I assume you understand what significance that holds.

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: This is only one blueprint amongst the things I wish to do, and at the very end of this pathway, Messengers will be able to overturn the barriers of culture and race. We can, with our own two hands, reach across this whole world.

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: I know, for all sorts of reasons, that in all probability this wouldn't come about. Race, culture, history, and from time to time Catastrophes adding to the mix.

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: Innumerous factors roiling around our strip of world have ensured the countries can't pull together as one.

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: Perhaps we must weather war, withstand Catastrophe. Perhaps this plan fundamentally cannot have a smooth ride within this split-up, estranged world of ours—

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: But that does not stand to forbid... the existence of bridges.

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: That being the case, we should try to part the great waves first.

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: By certain means, I've come to notice... the Apostle, the one and only, seems pretty open to this kind of thought exercise. Because of that, perhaps Laterano is our first step of a sorts in testing this new direction.

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: Cleric Hildegard?

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: No, sorry, I just never thought I'd be able to hear such things...

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Does your son know about this, erm, magnificent plan of yours?

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: Of course he doesn't. He still needs to polish himself. As I've said before, this project cannot be built in a day. I'm not the kind of person who rigs up bridges by his own hands. Maybe he is. Maybe, or maybe he isn't.

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: But he's my son, and that's enough.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Landen Monastery will assuredly find it a valuable experience, working in conjunction with your firm.

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: The honor is all mine, Cleric Hildegard.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: To tell the truth, Mr. Eurill, my own way of thinking is very simplistic. I adore my convent, and I believe the exemplary culture of Landen Monastery deserves to continue on.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: And so, I pray this will not spell its end.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: In comparison to your hopes, our motives may seem somewhat self-centered now.

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: Absolutely not, Cleric Hildegard. It's no small thing, wholeheartedly taking in and cherishing the homeland you adore.

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: —And you don't need to worry if this'll bring the Monastery much trouble. Landen Monastery stands only as Landen Monastery, nothing more.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Heheh, I didn't mean it like that. You have a lot on your mind, Mr. Eurill.

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: Nonsense. I should say that to you, Cleric Hildegard. Back when I was your age, I sure couldn't keep my head cool like yours.

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: It's gotten pretty late. We'll be getting a dinner party together for you tomorrow, Cleric Hildegard. Before that, you get some good shuteye.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Well, that went smoothly. What a mighty fellow.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Ugh, it feels like it's nothing to do with me now...
Just what can I do myself?
If only I knew.
Find some work? But how would I do that any faster...

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Wh—What... what's happening?

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Why does it turn out like this every time...?

steps.name: Croissant
steps.text: Ya ain't used to it yet?

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Used to becoming the focus of everyone's attention because of some unexpected explosion while we're on the way to a job?

steps.name: Croissant
steps.text: Slow down... I see him now! Thief! Get'cher behind back here!

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Oh, wow... is this really how you catch a thief...? I wonder what they stole that made it so serious...

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Who is it?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: It's me!

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Come in!

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Ah... I didn't disturb your rest, did I?

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Not at all. Is something the matter?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: It, it's just, um, I don't really know w-w-what to do on my own, because yesterday around this time I had my Miniature Cleaning Drone No. 23 to upgrade...

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Ah, um, yes, that's right, since I wanted to try out an even simpler Originium circuit, but in the end I set the curtains on fire... and, um...

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: *whimper*... I bought insurance... but now my card's balance is...

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: A—Alright, it's okay, you actually came at a good time. Do you recognize those people down there?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Down? Speaking of, it was really loud just now...

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Texas! They went your way.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: On 'em!

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Whoaaa... it's, it's all the Penguin Logistics girls...

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Ah. I think I've heard that name before.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Is it in their nature to... er, drift across the road to head off a car?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Uh, um, this happens often.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: It happens often, does it...

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Do you know their names?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Huh? Um, I do actually see a lot of them, for work...

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: The super handsome wolf who's driving, that's Texas. The really energetic lady chasing people with the hammer, she's Croissant...

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: (Neither seem like real names. Maybe I ought to start thinking too...)

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Ah, the cute lady who's trying to intervene right now is Sora... she used to be a really famous idol, but I'm guessing monasteries don't really hear about that stuff?

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: An idol?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Yep, um, singer, star, that sort of idea.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: A star...

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: The Monastery has its fair share of disciplines and taboos, but they aren't all that strict... at least, in the past few years, they haven't been.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: What does it feel like, to be a star?

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: I'd like to know too...

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Ah, the inn's intercity net TV should have recordings of her concerts available to broadcast. Why not see for yourself...?

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: The night's still young, after all.

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Th, then let's take a look... uh... you have to pay... oh? This one's a free program...
Truthfully, I've thought about it before.
Thought about the world outside, if it was nothing like I'd ever seen before.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Ah, it's so late already—

steps.name: Snowsant
steps.text: Zzz... zzz...

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Oh my...

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: My apologies... good night, Snowsant.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Yaawwn—

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Watching it actually woke me up...

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: TV, huh. The Monastery, I think, had a TV of its own...

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Through such a little rectangle, you can see across the whole world...

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: ...An idol...

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: No-no-no-what in Heaven's name am I thinking—

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Hm...

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: A Kazimierz Knight. That might not be too bad either... but those Majors always make you feel like something's off... if I have the chance, I should go see one.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Leithanien's Casters seem very well-regarded. I remember Angelica going off to Leithanien after she'd finished with us. I think she was pursuing further study at a music conservatory...?

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Sigh.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: The stars in the sky are so clear tonight.
The poets give the stars their words, the vagrants bare their million thoughts to the night. And me, I've already decided which star up there's gonna have my name.

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: Evenin', sister.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: A—And you are?

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: Oh, I saw you comin' outta my bar a minute ago. I was wrappin' up a little accident, see.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Er... Isn't that MountainDash Logistics's...

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: Eurill? Dumbass cow bought it and won't give it back, but you know what I'm sayin', I'm still that place's one and only bartender! I'm its soul!

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: Oh... hold up, hold up.

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: What? A fake? You got duped?

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: Then what're you waitin' for? Give their boat some fireworks! Yeah! That's what I said! What? 'course you gotta take me! What, you gonna leave me out?!

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: (No matter what this is, it has to be illegal, right—?!)

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: What did Eurill tell you?

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Why would I—

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: Nah, I know. Could only be gettin' some more hands on board, lookin' for a way out. Peace be to him.

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: It's a helluva world, shorty.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Why are you just—

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: But the way I see it now, you gotta think a little bigger.

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: Don't you worry, you're pretty easy on the eyes. My eyes. Even Paul Landen, handsome ass. I like it when he puts down his gun and picks up a pen!

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Found them, boss.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Wait—

steps.name: Emperor
steps.text: Waiting's a sucker's game! We got fools to huck in the river!

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Um...

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Paul Landen... the founder of the Monastery? What in the world was that strange little person trying...

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: What a brave new world.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Mr. Eurill, you'll have to forgive my manners, but before I leave Lungmen, there's something I must ask you.

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: By all means.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Why are you always in this bar?

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: Hah hah hah... I only just bought this place out from an acquaintance of mine. I quite fancy the atmosphere. It's not loud, it's not dirty, it's well-lit and strikes a vivid look.

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: Bars don't usually come like this, at least not in Lungmen. I don't know about Laterano... but I guess you probably don't see clerics in bars.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: It's not the total truth. Sundays in the convent's dormitories fundamentally aren't that different from a bar.

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: Hah hah, I think I understand now, why it is you and I can chat.

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: But the most important thing is, at some point, all of a sudden, I became very enamored with this bar's name—

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: —'The Ends of the Earth.'

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: At this very moment, we're at 'The Ends of the Earth.'

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: ...I see, then.

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: Well, to this project bringing the ideal to fruition. Cheers.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Cheers.

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: When are you setting off?

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: The plan was for tomorrow morning at nine.

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: Oh... did the plan change?

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: My mind changed.

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: Then regardless of what you're planning to do, will you need the assistance of our Messengers?

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: I won't. I didn't leave the Monastery this time just for one or two odds and ends, after all.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: What's more important is, I'm going to find where I can expand on my own faith.

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: I see. You've reached a conclusion?

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Hmm...

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: I'm hard-pressed to say it's a conclusion...

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: I'd love to see more of it. The world out there is... truthfully, a little more fascinating than I'd thought.

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: Now that's an answer with some youthful pep. I've got a small question too, and I'd like to seek a cleric's guidance.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: You flatter me. Please, ask away.

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: Do you think... that our project, even in the future, will truly be given others' recognition? Do you think the other voices of Laterano might stand on the other side to us?

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: The value of things shouldn't be decided prior to their coming. At the very least, we can choose to have some respect for all things and all creatures.

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: Is that a principle of the Monastery, too?

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Just Laterano nature. For that matter, Mr. Eurill, did you just want to test the present attitude of Landen Monastery?

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: Nonsense. I'm just curious what kind of heart my current collaborators bring to their work.

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: Obviously, I wouldn't doubt my own business. Thing is, once some things get beyond the scope of business, I have to start minding what other people think.

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: How do you see it?

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Landen Monastery tells a fable.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: They say, in a certain church in Laterano, there was a vast mural, depicting a story of heroes in ancient times, fighting for their faith.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Artists, from all over, all came to examine this mural. Some praised, some criticized, some chose to keep a rational quiet.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: —Then, from a small little quarter of Leithanien, came an upstart.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: The upstart was bloated, and unwilling to climb the church's stairs, thereupon he gazed at the church's window from afar. Through that window, he sighted a single deformed, vile beast in the artwork.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: And immediately, this businessman began to slander the mural, first saying that the hallowed and pure Laterano had produced such repulsive paintings, downright immoral.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Soon after, he spoke that even this single vile beast had a great many imperfections in the art.

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: Vile beast?

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Little did he realize that what he saw was not a vile beast in the mural, but a church ornament and a candleholder's silhouette, which by misfortune had given him such a mistaken impression.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: He couldn't even step into the grand church, yet dismantling what he saw in that superficial fragment, he came to an insight more superficial still.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Where do you think the problem arose from?

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: —Arrogance, and prejudice.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: So this fable is named 'La Bestia Superba.' If you should ask 'why did the church construct so high of a staircase?', that was indeed an arrogance in itself.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: What you want to do—that is to shatter all arrogance, or at the least, between every country, every land, every race's inharmonious arrogances, find a path, through the life mission of a Messenger.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: And between those, you even include the very arrogance of nature and life itself—Catastrophes.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: In realistic terms, I feel it will be very hard.

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: Someone's always got to be that stepping stone.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: This has eased my heart some.  When we're meant to talk money, we should talk it. But here, with you, Mr. Eurill, we're certainly talking of more than just money...

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: We're talking of quite a fair project. I feel a deep admiration for your ability to run things.

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: Hah hah hah, if that's how you think, then I'm completely and utterly relieved.

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: If you have the chance, why not take that son of mine on a trip to Laterano.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: But of course.

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: After all, ever since he came into contact with Mostima, I can see in his eyes, his idea of a 'Messenger' has grown a lot less narrow. Not bad—hm? What's that look for?

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: I feel like I've heard a name I can't quite let pass.

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: Oh? Was she that famous? I thought her reputation was pretty internal to the Messenger biz.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Well, ever since she was exiled, I haven't heard more about her, really.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Sankta can live very good lives wherever they are. After all, they're Sankta.

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: Hah hah, true words.

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: Right, Emperor wanted me to give you this.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Um? Emperor?

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: A very tenacious guy. He does everything off-script, but make no mistake, he's reliable.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: This is... a contact address? Is this a... company?

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Rho... Rhodes Island... Is that how you read it?

steps.name: Eurill
steps.text: Ah... once in a while, you trust Emperor's taste in associates. And you can trust me, they and this strip of world are marvelous one and the same.
